hilar lymphadenopathy, interstitial thickening, and perilymphatic ground glass opacities on Chest CT
worsening interstitial lung disease on follow-up Chest CT
restrictive disease with decreased diffusing capacity (33% predicted) on pulmonary function tests

concepts.why: The presence of anti-SSA (Ro) antibodies, hilar lymphadenopathy, interstitial lung disease, and characteristic skin biopsy findings support this diagnosis.
The combination of symmetric joint swelling, skin ulcers, elevated ferritin, and characteristic skin biopsy findings are consistent with this diagnosis.
The presence of anti-SSA (Ro) antibodies, interstitial lung disease, and joint involvement suggest this diagnosis.
The presence of anti-SSA (Ro) antibodies and characteristic skin biopsy findings support this diagnosis.
The presence of immunoglobulin G anticardiolipin antibodies, interstitial lung disease, and characteristic skin biopsy findings suggest this diagnosis.
The combination of symmetric joint swelling, skin ulcers, and elevated ferritin support this diagnosis.
The presence of hilar lymphadenopathy, interstitial thickening, and perilymphatic ground glass opacities on Chest CT support this diagnosis.
The presence of skin ulcers and characteristic skin biopsy findings support this diagnosis.
The presence of lymphocytopenia and elevated ferritin support this diagnosis.
The combination of symmetric joint swelling and skin ulcers support this diagnosis.

rationales.F04: Symmetric swelling of metacarpophalangeal joints is more typical of rheumatoid arthritis and dermatomyositis.
rationales.F08: Presence of anti-SSA (Ro) antibodies is highly specific for Sjögren's Syndrome.
rationales.F10: Worsening interstitial lung disease is a key feature of various connective tissue diseases, including systemic lupus erythematosus and mixed connective tissue disease.
rationales.F11: Restrictive disease with decreased diffusing capacity is indicative of interstitial lung disease, which can be seen in several connective tissue diseases.

frontier_selector.rationale: Positive anti-SSA (Ro) antibodies, hilar lymphadenopathy, interstitial lung disease, and symmetric joint swelling support Systemic Lupus Erythematosus, with Mixed Connective Tissue Disease as a close runner-up due to overlapping features but less comprehensive explanation of the patient's presentation.
